lines.trans: Since today is your birthday, Ms. Cindy, I thought it would be wonderful if we all gathered to celebrate together.
Your face is already small—how can you step behind me like that?! Only my face came out huge!
They look about the same size to me—besides, with your cap on, your face barely shows anyway.
How on earth is this similar—have you never even taken a photo with a woman, Producer?
Pardon? Ah yes—aside from family photos or group photos, not really…
I knew it—no wonder you are so clueless! When taking a photo with a woman, the guy is supposed to lean his face forward.
Since this photo must never leak out, I will take the memory card with me for now.
Ms. Cindy, do you happen to feel a little awkward or bored right now?
Well, I suppose a little bit.
Then hold on tight!

meanings.note: Basic verb of motion. With the respectful ending -세요 in 안녕히 가세요, it forms the polite farewell 'Goodbye!'. RR: gada.

examples.trans: I am going home.
Go safely!

meanings.note: Used as promissive polite (가져갈게요.).

examples.text: 이거 유출되면 안 되니까 일단 내가 가져갈게요.
examples.trans: Since this photo must never leak out, I will take the memory card with me for now.
Let us do that (will take it along) right away.

meanings.note: Used as compound noun + -이나 (가족사진이나).

examples.text: 예? 아 네, 가족사진이나 단체사진 말고는 별로…
examples.trans: Pardon? Ah yes—aside from family photos or group photos, not really…
This point about family photos or is really important.

meanings.note: Used in -(으)ㄴ/는 것 같다 to express 'it seems that...' or 'I think...'.

meanings.en: to be the same, to be like
meanings.note: Compares two things with -와/과 같다.

examples.trans: I think I'm late.
It looks like it's going to rain.

meanings.note: Adverb meaning 'together', often pronounced 가치.

examples.trans: Let's go together.
Let's go together. (2)

meanings.note: Bound noun often contracted to 거 in everyday speech.

examples.trans: This is my bag.
Because I think I'm late.

meanings.note: Honorific equivalent of 있다; used in 안녕히 계세요 ('goodbye' to someone staying).

examples.trans: Goodbye! (to someone staying)
Is the teacher inside right now?

meanings.note: adverb therefore

examples.trans: So let's go.
Therefore it is good.

그러다.gloss: to say so; to do so

meanings.en: to say so; to speak like that
meanings.note: contracted from 그러하다; often follows quoted speech

meanings.en: to do so; to act like that

examples.trans: Who said that?
That friend also said they are going together.

meanings.note: Colloquial contraction of 그러면.

examples.trans: Then let's meet tomorrow.
Then we're at the same company!

그렇다.gloss: to be so, to do so

meanings.en: to be like that, to be so
meanings.note: ㅎ-irregular; also used as a pro-verb ('do so / say so')

examples.trans: Is that really so?
Don't keep acting like that.

meanings.note: Used as adverb (꽉).

examples.trans: Then hold on tight!
I thought it over again (tightly, firmly).

meanings.note: Plain first-person singular pronoun used with friends, younger people, or subordinates; contracts to 난 with -는 and becomes 내가 before -가.

examples.trans: I'm going to stay home today.
I'll go first.

meanings.en: to appear, be published, be achieved (a score/result)
meanings.note: Used for ratings, test scores, or results coming out

examples.trans: I came outside from the house.
The exam results came out well.
Did you hear about this man?
I was busy today because of man.

meanings.note: Used as benefactive + -고 (내밀어주고).

examples.text: 그럴 줄 알았어, 그러니까 그렇게 눈치가 없지! 여자랑 찍을 땐 원래 남자가 좀 내밀어주고 그런 거예요.
examples.trans: I knew it—no wonder you are so clueless! When taking a photo with a woman, the guy is supposed to lean his face forward.
Let us do that (leans forward for her and) right away.

meanings.note: Standard polite affirmative response; also used to acknowledge that one is listening.

examples.trans: Ah, yes.
Yes, I understand.

examples.text: 보안이 너무 철저했나 봐. 정말 몰랐던 눈치야.
examples.trans: Our security must have been super tight. She genuinely had no idea.
The topic of sign, look of it came up during this shoot.

meanings.note: Placed before the verb it modifies.

examples.trans: I finished all my homework.
I ate all the rice.

meanings.note: Used as compound noun (단체사진).

examples.text: 예? 아 네, 가족사진이나 단체사진 말고는 별로…
examples.trans: Pardon? Ah yes—aside from family photos or group photos, not really…
This point about group photos is really important.

meanings.note: Takes a complement marked with 이/가.

examples.trans: I want to become a doctor.
It has already become 12 o'clock.

meanings.note: Used in spoken Korean dialogue (noun).

examples.text: 그래서 요 며칠 내 뒤를 졸졸 따라다니면서 선배를 떠봐?
examples.trans: So that is why you trailed behind me like a puppy these past few days sounding out your senior?
Here the word for 'behind me' is key.

meanings.en: to hold, to carry in one's hand
meanings.note: ㄹ-irregular verb; 들고 가다 means 'to carry along'.

examples.trans: Please take your bag with you.
If it's heavy, I'll carry it.

meanings.note: Often used as a bound noun after -(으)ㄹ to mean 'when' or 'while'.

examples.trans: Call me when you have time.
I lived in this neighborhood when I was young.

meanings.note: Auxiliary verb used after -지 to tell someone not to do something. Ending with -고 (말고) gives a brisk, trailing command. RR: malda.

examples.trans: Please do not worry.
Do not be late, and come early.

meanings.note: Intransitive/passive counterpart of 모으다 ('to gather/collect').

examples.trans: Everyone gathered in the meeting room.
Friends gather on the weekend.

meanings.note: Used as noun (모자).

examples.text: 안 된다니까, 괜히 돌아다니다가 아픈 데 덧나면 어떡해? 이거 타고 모자 쓰면 사람들이 못 알아본다고.
examples.trans: No walking—what if you wander around and make your injury worse? Ride this wheelchair with a cap on and nobody will recognize you.
This point about a cap is really important.
Did you hear about this not fond of?
I was busy today because of not fond of.
I want to is it visible? right now.
How about trying to is it visible? together tomorrow?
The atmosphere today is really is similar.
That person always looks is similar.

meanings.note: Pairs with the verb 찍다 ('to take/snap') in 사진을 찍다.

examples.trans: Shall we take a photo together?
This photo came out really well!

meanings.note: noun thought

examples.trans: Good idea.
Come to mind.

meanings.note: Used as noun + exclamatory copula (생일이네!).

examples.trans: Really? Today is your birthday! Happy day you were born!

examples.text: 그걸 내가 알았니? 준모야, 우리 저녁에 신디 생일 파티 해주자!
examples.trans: How was I supposed to know?! Joon-mo, let us throw Cindy a birthday party tonight!

meanings.note: Used as adjective + -지 (심심하지).

examples.text: 오늘 하루 종일 뭐 했어요? 심심하지 않았어요?
examples.trans: What did you do all day today—were you not bored?
It is really bored compared to what I expected.

meanings.note: Irregular ㅡ-stem verb: 쓰다 + -어 becomes 써.
Commonly used for tools, money, or time.

examples.trans: I write in my diary every night.
I wrote my name on the very first page of the book.
Did you hear about this Ms.?
I was busy today because of Ms..

meanings.note: Expresses sudden realization, surprise, or hesitation.

examples.trans: Ah, yes.
Oh, I see!

meanings.note: Used in spoken Korean dialogue (adv).

examples.text: 아무래도 미래의 의사다 보니까 공부할 것도 많고.
examples.trans: Well, since I am a future doctor, I have a ton of studying to do.
Here the word for 'after all, naturally' is key.

meanings.note: Short-form negation placed directly before verbs and adjectives

examples.trans: I'm not going to the office today.
I haven't watched that movie yet.

meanings.note: Used in standard farewells 안녕히 계세요 and 안녕히 가세요.

examples.trans: Goodbye! (to someone staying)
Goodbye! (to someone leaving)

않다.gloss: to not do, to not be

meanings.en: to not do, to not be
meanings.note: Auxiliary negative verb/adjective used after -지 (long-form negation)

examples.trans: The weather isn't cold today.
I didn't say anything.

meanings.note: ㄹ-irregular verb: stem 알- drops ㄹ before ㄴ, ㅂ, ㅅ (e.g., 압니까)

examples.trans: Do you know that person's phone number?
Yes, I know well.

meanings.en: what to do, how to act
meanings.note: Contraction of 어떻게 하다.

examples.trans: What should we do?
What should we do? (2)
How did you get here?
How should we solve this problem?

meanings.note: Used as disjunctive -거나 (어색하거나).

examples.text: 신디 씨, 혹시 지금 좀 어색하거나 심심하십니까?
examples.trans: Ms. Cindy, do you happen to feel a little awkward or bored right now?
It is really awkward or compared to what I expected.

meanings.note: Used in spoken Korean dialogue (adv).

examples.trans: Stop, that is enough—it was all a lie anyway!
Here the word for 'anyway, in any case' is key.
Did you hear about this face, though?
I was busy today because of face, though.

없다.gloss: to not exist, to not have

meanings.en: to not exist, to not be present

examples.trans: I don't have time right now.
The tickets are all sold out, so there aren't any.
Did you hear about this female?
I was busy today because of female.

meanings.note: Slightly more formal/deferential variant of 네, commonly used when speaking to a boss or superior.

examples.trans: Yes, understood.

meanings.note: The present day; often used adverbially without a particle.

examples.trans: The weather is nice today.

examples.trans: Just leave him alone, he is completely wasted.
That's right, Cindy turned out to be a total fan of good looks.

meanings.note: describes how things typically work
refers to an initial state or plan

examples.trans: Traffic is usually heavy on Mondays.
This place was originally a park.

meanings.note: Used as passive conditional (유출되면).

examples.text: 이거 유출되면 안 되니까 일단 내가 가져갈게요.

examples.trans: How much is this?

Test2

좋다.gloss: to be good, to be nice

examples.trans: I feel really good today.
It's nice to take a walk in the morning.

meanings.note: When used with 알다/모르다, it means knowing or not knowing a fact or how to do something.

examples.trans: I knew it would rain.
Do you know how to swim?
What time is it now?
I'll leave right now.

meanings.en: to film, to shoot, to take (a photo)
meanings.note: Used for capturing photos or video.

examples.trans: Did you happen to film this just now too?

meanings.note: Used as experiential polite question (찍어봤어요?).

examples.text: 이게 어떻게 비슷해? 피디님 여자랑 사진도 안 찍어봤어요?

meanings.note: Used as noun + object (축하를).

examples.trans: She prepared for the exam to become a variety PD.

meanings.en: to do, to perform, to hold
meanings.note: Core verb; also combines with nouns to form verbs.

examples.trans: What are you doing right now?
We are holding a meeting today.

meanings.note: Softens a question or expresses uncertainty.

examples.trans: Did you happen to film this just now too?
Do you happen to have time?
